summary: EIC-684B is an interactive, accessible web oscilloscope that translates NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations into real-time 4-channel musical sonifications. Inspired by 1990s Tektronix laboratory hardware, it eliminates visual clutter and turns Earth science frames into harmonious C-minor pentatonic soundscapes alongside four live waveforms and frequency telemetry. Users can scan datasets along three spatial axes (0° longitude, 90° latitude, and 45° diagonal) or upload custom images. Designed with accessibility first, EIC-684B features a built-in TalkBack voice mode (T key), full arrow-key navigation, live aria-live logs, and one-click spoken summaries so blind and low-vision users can independently explore planetary data.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

EIC-684B ("Earth Sonification Scope") transforms NASA EIC visual frames into multi-sensory, real-time audio experiences. Each image is processed client-side on an HTML5 Canvas into 64 spatial slices along a user-selectable scan axis (0° Left-to-Right for longitude, 90° Top-to-Bottom for latitude/climate zones, or 45° Diagonal). Pixels are converted from RGB to HSV and mapped onto a harmonious C-minor pentatonic scale using the Web Audio API:

- CH1 (Yellow Trace — Warmth / Lights): Maps red, orange, and yellow regions (thermal currents, city lights) to higher pitches and brighter amplitudes.

- CH2 (Green Trace — Biosphere / Mid-spectrum): Maps green bands to balanced mid-range tones.

- CH3 (Pink Trace — Luminance & Density): Modulates a global lowpass filter and adds harmonic shimmer for bright clusters.

- CH4 (Cyan Trace — Oceans / Cold): Maps blue tones to calm, low-frequency foundation drones.

Each channel routes through an independent AnalyserNode to render four authentic real-time waveforms on a Tektronix TDS-684B-inspired CRT display, allowing users to solo or mute any layer (keys 1–4).

Benefits, Impact & Accessibility Considerations:

Scientific visualizations often exclude blind and low-vision audiences. Beyond standard screen-reader support (aria-live status logs and a one-click Voice Desc summary), we built an integrated TalkBack mode (press T) with full arrow-key navigation and audio confirmation of every button state. Users can explore climate patterns purely by ear, without requiring external assistive software.

Tools, Languages & Creativity:

Built 100% client-side with zero external dependencies using HTML5 Canvas, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript (ES Modules), Web Audio API, and Web Speech API (SpeechSynthesis), deployed via GitHub Pages. Instead of generic neon dashboards, the 1990s laboratory oscilloscope metaphor makes every visual control directly correspond to a physical signal channel.

Live App: https://evgeniyak2008.github.io/earth-sonification-scope/

Source Code: https://github.com/EvgeniyaK2008/earth-sonification-scope

SI / AI Disclosure:

An AI coding assistant was used during development to assist with JavaScript/CSS code structuring, Web Audio optimization, and English documentation. All NASA data, creative direction, accessibility workflow, and final integration were directed and verified by the participant.
